svg.aria-label: Conduct a retrospective social network analysis (SNA) of intersectoral networks mobilized in primary care from CLSC territories to address the concurrent social and healthcare needs of different profiles of older people living at home, in order to characterize their composition, the structure of their relationships, and the nature and intensity of collaboration between actors.

text.tspan: Methodological objective 3
Conduct a retrospective social network analysis (SNA) of intersectoral networks mobilized in primary care from CLSC territories
to address the concurrent social and healthcare needs of different profiles of older people living at home, in order to characterize
their composition, the structure of their relationships, and the nature and intensity of collaboration between actors.
Instrument: one relational questionnaire administered once to
organizational actors about the previous 12 months; a few
supplementary open questions, without separate interviews.
Ties: partner organizations, referrals, information exchange,
coordination and joint decisions; direction, frequency, reported
reciprocity and relevant need profiles.
Whole networks by profile: ties among all organizations within
each territorial boundary; composition, structure and operating
arrangements, subject to coverage.
Ego networks: partners of focal organizations or teams, including
the CLSC; size, diversity and ego–alter ties. Alter–alter ties require
explicit collection.
Design: quantitative observational, descriptive and comparative
study; cross-sectional collection with 12-month retrospective recall
and no assigned intervention.
Connection: both SNA levels use the same questionnaire. Open
answers contextualize findings; no sequential or convergent
mixed-methods design is planned.
